items.text: Morph on a slider. In the Index, the handles of the continuous sound and dice sliders (Favourite holds, Repeat the step before, Air, Space, Tail, Timbre, Grain, Morph, Tempo drifts, Holds and repeats, Pauses) now carry a +. Hold the handle and the slider stays put while a section opens below with Motion (Still, Ping-pong, Sweep, Drift), Speed (Slow, Medium, Fast) and Span (Small, Wide, Full). The + turns to a - while it is open, hold again to close. The handle's mark is grey, and turns to the accent while the slider is set to move. Two dots on the track show the reach of the swing, a faint one marks the centre. Drag the slider, or double-tap its name, and the swing re-centres there. Your settings are kept.
Structural sliders (Size, Colours, Tempo) have no morph. The heads-up display sliders do not have it yet.
The corner triangle on a lit button (the headphones, the MIDI plug) no longer turns into a stray wedge: the yellow edge bar is whole and the triangle sits beside it.
Choosing a binaural mode, source or level in the heads-up display no longer jumps the panel's scroll. The chips are updated where they stand instead of being rebuilt on every tap.
The tempo nudge buttons that appear when you drag the metronome (-10, -1, +1, +10) are small circles, about half their old size.

The Haitian djouba study now plays its own drums. Opening it loads a "Haitian djouba drums" sound set: the kata (stick on wood), the boula (small goatskin drum), the manman (large goatskin drum) and the tchatcha shaker, one per track. Before, its tracks played the generic drum kit, so the goatskin drums did not sound like goatskin. The four drums are also in the colour menus as "Djouba: ...". They are synthesized sketches from descriptions, not heard by a drummer. The Lebanese study still plays the generic kit; its own drums come with the Lebanese kit.

The sliders in the Index now look and behave like the ones in the heads-up display: a thin track, the readout turns to the accent colour once you change a slider, and double-tapping the slider's name glides it back to its default. On Size, the name's double-tap is the same as the Default grid button.
New "Default grid (12 × 12)" button under Size. Importing a MIDI piece makes the grid 16 × 16 and leaves it that way; one tap puts it back to the standard 12 × 12 and clears the imported piece.

New sound kit: Haitian rara. Pick "Haitian rara" in the sound sets to load eight synthesized voices, one per colour: three bamboo vaksin trumpets and a fourth a little over a semitone above the third, a tin kone horn, a goatskin tanbou with its slap, a kata stick with a kes rattle, and a graj scraper with tcha-tcha and a faint whistle.

The vaksin are tuned by offsets from a centre of 220 Hz (0, +310, +590 and +690 cents), not a standard scale, and each always sounds at its own pitch whatever row it lands on. They are sketches from published descriptions of rara, not a transcription, and I have not had them heard by a rara player.
Each voice is also on its own in the colour menus, as "Rara: ...".

Colours and marks are now checkboxes. Tap to add or remove one (one always stays on); tap twice quickly to choose just that one. Drawing with several on deals from them, as a shuffled bag by default: every chosen colour or mark comes up before any repeats, so a stroke is evenly mixed. A small shuffle button appears when you have more than one on; press it to pick at random instead.
Saved looks carry the chosen colours, marks and deal order.
Hold's rings are bolder and travel farther, and they appear only while a held sound is actually sounding. With Hold on and nothing held, the hand stays still.
